newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says troops kill three Iraq-based rebels.
newsitem.headline: Iran says troops kill three Iraq-based rebels.

text.p: Security forces in central Iran clashed with four members of an Iraq-based armed opposition group, killing three and wounding another, state-run Tehran radio said on Monday.

It said intelligence (internal security) ministry agents arrested the fourth Mujahideen Khalq member and found pistols, grenades and other military weapons "bearing Iraqi army labels" in the group's safe house in Isfahan, 300 km (185 miles) south of Tehran. It did not say when the clash occurred.
Tehran has said its troops killed more than 20 Mujahideen members, who it said had come from neighbouring Iraq, in clashes in western and northern Iran in the past few weeks.

The Mujahideen have admitted that some of their forces, who they said belonged to underground cells in Iran, were killed. But the group said its fighters had slain or wounded "hundreds" of government troops.
Iran has not reported any casualties among its forces.
Tehran has blamed the group, which has several camps in Iraq near the Iranian border, for cross-border attacks and bombings in the past few years.
The Mujahideen have denied attacking civilians, but have taken responsibility for hitting military, government and military targets.
Iran and Iraq, which fought a war from 1980 to 1988, often accuse each other of backing rebel groups from the other country.
